content.text: create an advanced procedurally generated 3d game in a single self-contained html page, feel free to use http-loaded dependencies/libraries from unpkg/etc. aim for stunning visuals

Advanced procedurally generated 3D game.
Single self-contained HTML page.
External libraries via CDN (unpkg, etc.) allowed.
Stunning visuals.

    *   *Engine:* Three.js is the industry standard for web-based 3D. It's powerful, well-documented, and supports shaders.
    *   *Procedural Generation:* Perlin Noise or Simplex Noise for terrain/structures.
    *   *Visuals:* Bloom effect (Post-processing), Dynamic lighting, Particle systems, Gradient skies.
    *   *Gameplay:* A "Flight/Exploration" experience is usually the most visually rewarding for procedural generation (endless terrain).

    *   *Concept:* "Neon Void Explorer." A futuristic flight simulator where you glide over an infinite, procedurally generated neon landscape.
    *   *Mechanics:*
        *   Player moves forward automatically.
        *   WASD/Arrows for steering.
        *   Infinite terrain generation based on noise.
        *   Collectibles (rings/orbs) for points.
        *   Speed boost.

    *   *Terrain:* Use a plane geometry. Displace vertices using Simplex Noise. To make it infinite, use a "chunk" system or shift the plane and update vertices. *Decision: Shifting a large plane and updating noise based on world-position in a shader is most performant.*
    *   *Visuals:*
        *   Dark background.
        *   Emissive neon materials.
        *   Bloom pass to make the neon glow.
        *   Fog to hide the edge of the world.
        *   Starfield background.

    *   *HTML Structure:* Basic container, overlay for UI (Score, Speed).
    *   *CSS:* Minimal, full screen, hidden overflow, futuristic font.
    *   *JS - Three.js Setup:* Scene, Camera, Renderer (WebGLRenderer).
    *   *JS - Lighting:* Ambient light + a Point light attached to the player for local glow.
    *   *JS - Noise:* Import `simplex-noise` or implement a simple one.
    *   *JS - The Terrain:* Create a large grid. Use a Custom Shader Material for the terrain to handle the "infinite" movement on the GPU (this is much faster than updating 10,000 vertices per frame on the CPU).

    *   *Vertex Shader:* Calculate height based on `position.x + time` and `position.z + time`.
    *   *Fragment Shader:* Color based on height (blue for low, purple/pink for high). Add a "grid" line effect.

    *   *Controls:* Simple `keydown`/`keyup` listeners.
    *   *Movement:* Update camera position and rotate slightly based on input.
    *   *Game Loop:* `requestAnimationFrame`. Update time uniforms for the shader.

    *   *Issue:* Basic Three.js materials look flat.
    *   *Fix:* Add `UnrealBloomPass` from Three.js examples.
    *   *Issue:* Terrain might look repetitive.
    *   *Fix:* Layer multiple octaves of noise.

    *   *Check:* Is it one file? Yes.
    *   *Check:* Are dependencies external? Yes (Three.js, SimplexNoise, Postprocessing).
    *   *Check:* Visuals? Neon, Bloom, Infinite.
